ledger.x: 1787: Ali Pasha takes the Sanjak of Trikala and, in 1787 or 1788, seizes Ioannina: "This marked the beginning of the Pashalik of Yanina."
1789: Ali's first invasion of Souli; further campaigns in 1790, 1792, 1800 and 1802.
1789-1791: Ali takes Konitsa, Libohovë, Përmet and Tepelenë "from Avlona" and Arta, "giving access to the Ionian Sea via the Gulf of Arta".
1792: Muhtar's appointments "stretch[ed] for the first time Ali's control down to Livadia and the Gulf of Corinth".
October 1798: Ali seizes Butrint, Igoumenitsa, Preveza and Vonitsa "from the French"; "Parga stayed French".
1799: Himara annexed after the 1797 raid in which "more than 6,000 civilians" were killed.
1802: Ali takes Delvinë.
1803: Souli falls; the Ali page says the Souliotes departed and their villages were destroyed after his autumn attack.
1803: the Souliote War ends with the conquest of Souli.
1806: Ali "finally managed to gain control of Karli-Eli"; invaded in October 1789 but the Ottomans granted it to Mihrişah Valide Sultan, so it was not annexed until 1806.
1807: "Veli ruled Morea (Peloponnese), which was incorporated" (1807-1812).
1809: Berat falls to Ali's family.
1810: Ali takes the rest of the Sanjak of Avlona, "stretching his dominion from Durrës in the north to Arta in the south".
1811: Gjirokastër "surrendered after a show of force".
1812: end of Veli's rule in the Morea ("1807-1812").
1819: "Parga acquired from the British and annexed to Delvina"; the inhabitants fled to Corfu.
ledger.cpn: United States of the Ionian Islands

ledger.x: 1820: Berat goes to Mustafa Pasha Bushati of Scutari; the Mustafa page does not say from whom, and Ali Pasha, declared a rebel in 1820, held Berat since 1809, so the Pashalik of Yanina is the counterpart by the researcher's reading.

1820: "After being declared a rebel in 1820"; the Yanina page: Mahmud II ordered his deposition, Ali resisted and formed a coalition with the Souliotes on 4 December 1820, with "some 20,000 Turkish troops" against his army.
24 January 1822: Ali Pasha is killed by Ottoman agents and his head sent to the Sultan.
January 1822: Ali Pasha "(1743 - 24 January 1822)"; the pashalik becomes the Ioannina Eyalet.

wars.name: Souliote War
wars.outcome: Ali invaded in 1789 and again in 1790, 1792, 1800 and 1802; peace in 1792 returned captured villages; Souli was conquered in 1803 and the Souliotes left.

wars.name: Ottoman campaign against Ali Pasha
wars.outcome: Ali was declared a rebel in 1820, resisted with some 50,000 Albanian troops available to him, and was assassinated on 24 January 1822; the pashalik ended.

certainty.note: A de facto independent pashalik that "was never officially recognized"; no treaty frontier.
